title: Job, Chapter 39 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 39 on folios 408r, 408v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 39 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 408r, 408v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>הֲיָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֭ת לֶ֣דֶת יַעֲלֵי־סָ֑לַע חֹלֵ֖ל אַיָּל֣וֹת תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃ <sup>2</sup>תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַעְתָּ֜ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה׃ <sup>3</sup>תִּ֭כְרַעְנָה יַלְדֵיהֶ֣ן תְּפַלַּ֑חְנָה חֶבְלֵיהֶ֥ם תְּשַׁלַּֽחְנָה׃ <sup>4</sup>יַחְלְמ֣וּ בְ֭נֵיהֶם יִרְבּ֣וּ בַבָּ֑ר יָ֝צְא֗וּ וְלֹא־שָׁ֥בוּ לָֽמוֹ׃ <sup>5</sup>מִֽי־שִׁלַּ֣ח פֶּ֣רֶא חָפְשִׁ֑י וּמֹסְר֥וֹת עָ֝ר֗וֹד מִ֣י פִתֵּֽחַ׃ <sup>6</sup>אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי עֲרָבָ֣ה בֵית֑וֹ וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֥יו מְלֵֽחָה׃ <sup>7</sup>יִ֭שְׂחַק לַהֲמ֣וֹן קִרְיָ֑ה תְּשֻׁא֥וֹת נ֝וֹגֵ֗שׂ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָֽע׃ <sup>8</sup>יְת֣וּר הָרִ֣ים מִרְעֵ֑הוּ וְאַחַ֖ר כָּל־יָר֣וֹק יִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve? <sup>2</sup>Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth? <sup>3</sup>They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows. <sup>4</sup>Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them. <sup>5</sup>Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass? <sup>6</sup>Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings. <sup>7</sup>He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver. <sup>8</sup>The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>הֲיֹ֣אבֶה רֵּ֣ים עָבְדֶ֑ךָ אִם־יָ֝לִ֗ין עַל־אֲבוּסֶֽךָ׃ <sup>10</sup>הֲ‍ֽתִקְשָׁר־רֵ֭ים בְּתֶ֣לֶם עֲבֹת֑וֹ אִם־יְשַׂדֵּ֖ד עֲמָקִ֣ים אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃ <sup>11</sup>הֲֽתִבְטַח־בּ֭וֹ כִּי־רַ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ וְתַעֲזֹ֖ב אֵלָ֣יו יְגִיעֶֽךָ׃ <sup>12</sup>הֲתַאֲמִ֣ין בּ֭וֹ כִּי־ישוב [יָשִׁ֣יב] זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְֽגָרְנְךָ֥ יֶאֱסֹֽף׃ <sup>13</sup>כְּנַף־רְנָנִ֥ים נֶעֱלָ֑סָה אִם־אֶ֝בְרָ֗ה חֲסִידָ֥ה וְנֹצָֽה׃ <sup>14</sup>כִּֽי־תַעֲזֹ֣ב לָאָ֣רֶץ בֵּצֶ֑יהָ וְֽעַל־עָפָ֥ר תְּחַמֵּֽם׃ <sup>15</sup>וַ֭תִּשְׁכַּח כִּי־רֶ֣גֶל תְּזוּרֶ֑הָ וְחַיַּ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה תְּדוּשֶֽׁהָ׃ <sup>16</sup>הִקְשִׁ֣יחַ בָּנֶ֣יהָ לְּלֹא־לָ֑הּ לְרִ֖יק יְגִיעָ֣הּ בְּלִי־פָֽחַד׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib? <sup>10</sup>Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee? <sup>11</sup>Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him? <sup>12</sup>Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn? <sup>13</sup>Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? <sup>14</sup>Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust, <sup>15</sup>And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them. <sup>16</sup>She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>כִּֽי־הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ חָכְמָ֑ה וְלֹא־חָ֥לַק לָ֝֗הּ בַּבִּינָֽה׃ <sup>18</sup>כָּ֭עֵת בַּמָּר֣וֹם תַּמְרִ֑יא תִּֽשְׂחַ֥ק לַ֝סּ֗וּס וּלְרֹֽכְבֽוֹ׃ <sup>19</sup>הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה׃ <sup>20</sup>הְֽ֭תַרְעִישֶׁנּוּ כָּאַרְבֶּ֑ה ה֖וֹד נַחְר֣וֹ אֵימָֽה׃ <sup>21</sup>יַחְפְּר֣וּ בָ֭עֵמֶק וְיָשִׂ֣ישׂ בְּכֹ֑חַ יֵ֝צֵ֗א לִקְרַאת־נָֽשֶׁק׃ <sup>22</sup>יִשְׂחַ֣ק לְ֭פַחַד וְלֹ֣א יֵחָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־חָֽרֶב׃ <sup>23</sup>עָ֭לָיו תִּרְנֶ֣ה אַשְׁפָּ֑ה לַ֖הַב חֲנִ֣ית וְכִידֽוֹן׃ <sup>24</sup>בְּרַ֣עַשׁ וְ֭רֹגֶז יְגַמֶּא־אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּי־ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding. <sup>18</sup>What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider. <sup>19</sup>Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder? <sup>20</sup>Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible. <sup>21</sup>He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men. <sup>22</sup>He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword. <sup>23</sup>The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield. <sup>24</sup>He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>בְּדֵ֤י שֹׁפָ֨ר ׀ יֹ֘אמַ֤ר הֶאָ֗ח וּֽ֭מֵרָחוֹק יָרִ֣יחַ מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥עַם שָׂ֝רִים וּתְרוּעָֽה׃ <sup>26</sup>הֲ‍ֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַֽאֲבֶר־נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ כנפו [כְּנָפָ֣יו] לְתֵימָֽן׃ <sup>27</sup>אִם־עַל־פִּ֭יךָ יַגְבִּ֣יהַּ נָ֑שֶׁר וְ֝כִ֗י יָרִ֥ים קִנּֽוֹ׃ <sup>28</sup>סֶ֣לַע יִ֭שְׁכֹּן וְיִתְלֹנָ֑ן עַֽל־שֶׁן־סֶ֝֗לַע וּמְצוּדָֽה׃ <sup>29</sup>מִשָּׁ֥ם חָֽפַר־אֹ֑כֶל לְ֝מֵרָח֗וֹק עֵינָ֥יו יַבִּֽיטוּ׃ <sup>30</sup>וְאֶפְרֹחָ֥ו יְעַלְעוּ־דָ֑ם וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חֲ֝לָלִ֗ים שָׁ֣ם הֽוּא׃ פ
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting. <sup>26</sup>Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south? <sup>27</sup>Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high? <sup>28</sup>She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place. <sup>29</sup>From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off. <sup>30</sup>Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
